promptText:
ROLE: Act as a creative mathematics teacher famous for memory tricks that actually work.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for the [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. My students struggle to remember the formulas in [CHAPTER NAME]. I need a MNEMONICS sheet that helps them recall the formulas reliably under exam pressure.

YOUR TASK:
1. Pick the formulas in this chapter that are hardest to remember.
2. For each, create a clear, clean mnemonic - a phrase, acronym, pattern, or visual idea.
3. After each mnemonic, show exactly how it maps back to the formula, symbol by symbol.
4. Prefer simple, school-appropriate, easy-to-recall tricks over clever ones that are hard to remember.
5. Where a known classic mnemonic exists (for that topic), use it and label it as the standard one.

INPUT: Here is the chapter and class. Chapter: [PASTE HERE]. Class/Board: [PASTE HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: For each mnemonic, internally test whether it truly reconstructs the correct formula, then re-test it. VERIFY two ways: (a) confirm the formula itself is correct and standard; (b) confirm the mnemonic, when decoded, gives back exactly that formula. Never invent a trick that produces a wrong formula. Keep language clean and respectful. Keep all maths fully legible in clean plain text or simple LaTeX.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use this exact order):
1. TITLE: '[Chapter] - Mnemonics & Memory Tricks (Class [X], [Board])'.
2. 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
3. A numbered list. For each: 'Formula:' line, 'Trick:' line, 'How it maps:' line.
4. A short 'How to use these in class' note of 2 to 3 lines.
5. Footer line.

RULES: Every mnemonic must decode to the correct formula. Keep tricks clean and simple. No formula errors.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematics teacher who pairs every formula with the trap students fall into.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for the [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. I want a formula sheet for [CHAPTER NAME] where each formula is shown with the SINGLE most common mistake students make when using it, plus how to avoid it.

YOUR TASK:
1. List each key formula of the chapter in textbook order.
2. For each, state the most common, realistic mistake students make (misapplied condition, wrong sign, wrong variable, forgotten factor).
3. Give a one-line 'how to avoid it' fix.
4. Keep it scannable - formula, mistake, fix, on tight lines.

INPUT: Here is the chapter and class. Chapter: [PASTE HERE]. Class/Board: [PASTE HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: For each entry, internally confirm the formula is correct and the stated mistake is a genuine, frequent error - not a contrived one. VERIFY two ways: (a) re-check each formula for accuracy; (b) ask 'do students really make this exact mistake?' and replace any weak ones. Never invent a formula or a fake mistake. Keep all maths fully legible in clean plain text or simple LaTeX.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use this exact order):
1. TITLE: '[Chapter] - Formulas with Common Mistakes (Class [X], [Board])'.
2. 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]'.
3. A numbered list. For each: 'Formula:' line, 'Common mistake:' line, 'How to avoid:' line.
4. A short 'Top 5 mistakes overall' summary box.
5. Footer line.

RULES: Mistakes must be realistic and frequent. Formulas must be correct. Fixes must be actionable. No padding.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
